decision.rule: adopt the larger setting only if the paired mean log10 test rollout-16 ratio over cells x arms <= -0.0414 and better on a majority of cells (09 contract v2)
decision.outcome: width 128 -> 256 at 128k steps adopted (mean paired dlog10 -0.108, 95% CI -0.164 to -0.052, better on 12 of 12 cells over 33 pairs); steps 128k -> 256k at 128 x 4 not adopted (mean +0.023, CI -0.017 to +0.064, better on 3 of 9 cells over 20 pairs); the threshold -0.0414 lies outside both intervals (no marginal-band decision). The S1 -> S2b comparison (256k steps at 256 x 4) has no data: its units (40-80+ min) could not survive the compute regime below; the S0 -> S1 result at width 128 and the checkpoint positions at S2a (mean fraction 0.58, median 0.62, 31% in the last tenth, no divergence) stand for the horizon check. The audit was read before its finals completed (S0 74/80, S1 20/80, S2a 36/80 instances) because every further hour of audit packs delayed the finals by the same hour.
decision.compute_regime: the free tier preempts long jobs; packs of the finals run short walls; a unit starts only if its arm's reserve fits before the deadline; the 256k-step settings are not runnable this way.

stragglers.what: the 627 L2 trial units (of 32,256) still pending at that point run under torch.set_flush_denormal(True), and the finals of a cell whose winner trial was flushed share its numerics; every such record carries flush_denormal: true; every other arm never flushes
stragglers.cause: subnormal floats in the gradients of a collapsed L2 trial (penalty strength >= 0.1): 32-62 ms per step instead of 5.4 ms, so a 128k-step unit needs about two hours and no free_qos pack survives that long
evidence: external/analysis/flush_check/ (paired runs of the same unit with and without the flush)
checks: flush-to-zero only in the L2 arm, recorded per unit
no mixed cell: a flushed winner's finals are all flushed, an unflushed winner's finals all unflushed
